source: Technology Promotion Project to Increase Productivity Around Tonle Sap (TSTD — TA 7305-CAM), watermelon (ដំណាំឪឡឹក) technical training booklet, prepared by the project's agricultural techniques and extension officer in cooperation with East West Seed International, November 2016. Contact: livleanghy@gmail.com
text:
Mites (ចែ) attack watermelon leaves, typically noticeable as fine webbing and feeding damage on the underside of leaves, especially during the dry season. Under heavy infestation, affected leaves show yellow speckling/stippling and can eventually dry out and drop.

Recommended control measures: cut off and remove heavily infested leaves, either burying or burning them away from the field rather than leaving them nearby; and apply agricultural pesticides such as Abamectin (Abermectin), Dinotefuran, or Fipronil.

General pesticide-use cautions given alongside the pest sections in the source: do not mix different agricultural pesticides together for spraying; select the pesticide appropriate to the specific pest to avoid unnecessary risk; and spray pesticide in the morning, directing the spray onto the underside of the leaves where air circulation is good, for better coverage and effectiveness.
